facts.statement: The type specimens of Liliensternus were discovered near Großer Gleichberg in Thuringia, Germany.
facts.quote: The specimens of Liliensternus, designated as the syntype series HMN BM.R.2175, were recovered near Großer Gleichberg in the Trossingen Formation of the Middle Keuper Group in Thuringia, Germany

facts.statement: Count Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern discovered the type specimens in the winter of 1932/1933.
facts.quote: The syntypes were discovered by Count Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern in the winter of 1932/1933

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene described Liliensternus in 1934.
facts.quote: Liliensternus was described by Friedrich von Huene in 1934

facts.statement: Fragmentary remains suggest that adult Liliensternus could have reached lengths of 7 to 9 meters.
facts.quote: possible fragmentary remains indicate an adult length of 7 to 9 meters

facts.statement: Liliensternus is the best-represented Triassic theropod from Europe and one of the largest known.
facts.quote: It is the best represented Triassic theropod from Europe and one of the largest known

facts.statement: Liliensternus was approximately 5.15 meters long and may have weighed about 127 kilograms.
facts.quote: Liliensternus was approximately 5.15 m long, and may have weighed about 127 kg

facts.statement: In Liliensternus, the tibia is 409 mm long and the femur is 440 mm long.
facts.quote: The tibia (409 mm) is shorter than the femur (440 mm) in both Dilophosaurus and Liliensternus

facts.statement: Many reconstructions depict Liliensternus with a crest similar to that of Dilophosaurus, though the skull is not well known.
facts.quote: Although the skull is not well known, many reconstructions have Liliensternus with a crest similar to that observed in Dilophosaurus

facts.statement: Liliensternus was an active bipedal carnivore that likely preyed on large herbivores like Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: Liliensternus was an active bipedal carnivore that could have preyed on the larger herbivores like Plateosaurus

facts.statement: Liliensternus is classified as a basal member of the Neotheropoda.
facts.quote: Originally assigned to the Halticosauridae, Liliensternus is today considered a basal member of the Neotheropoda

facts.statement: It is debated whether Liliensternus airelensis should remain in Liliensternus or be assigned to the separate genus Lophostropheus.
facts.quote: in 2007, Martin Ezcurra and Cuny assigned the material to its own genus, Lophostropheus

facts.statement: The name Liliensternus honors Count Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern, an amateur paleontologist and medical doctor.
facts.quote: The genus and specific names Liliensternus liliensterni are derived from the last name of count, amateur paleontologist, and medical doctor, Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern

facts.statement: Liliensternus was estimated to be approximately 5.15 meters long and weigh around 127 kilograms.
facts.quote: Liliensternus tenía aproximadamente 5,15 metros de largo, y puede haber pesado alrededor de 127 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Other estimates suggest Liliensternus could have reached a maximum length of 5.20 meters and a maximum weight of 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: Otras estimaciones sugieren que Liliensternus tenía como máximo 5,20 metros de largo y pesaba 200 kilogramos como máximo.

facts.statement: Although the skull is not well known, many reconstructions depict Liliensternus with a crest similar to that of Dilophosaurus.
facts.quote: Aunque el cráneo no se conoce bien, muchas reconstrucciones muestran a Liliensternus con una cresta similar a la observada en Dilophosaurus.

facts.statement: Liliensternus had an unusually short ilium, similar to the condition seen in Dilophosaurus.
facts.quote: Su ilion, hueso de la cadera, es inusualmente corto, como es el caso de Dilophosaurus.

facts.statement: The syntypes of Liliensternus were discovered by Count Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern in the winter of 1932–1933 in marl deposits from the Late Triassic Norian stage, approximately 228 to 208 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los sintipos fueron descubiertos por el conde Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern en el invierno de 1932 a 1933 en marl, una lutita rica en cal, depositada en la etapa noriana del período Triásico Tardío, hace aproximadamente entre 228 a 208 millones de años.

facts.statement: Liliensternus was described by Friedrich von Huene in 1934.
facts.quote: Liliensternus fue descrito por Friedrich von Huene en 1934.

facts.statement: The genus and species name Liliensternus liliensterni are derived from the surname of Count Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern, an amateur paleontologist and doctor.
facts.quote: El género y los nombres específicos Liliensternus liliensterni se derivan del apellido del conde, paleontólogo aficionado y médico, Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was named in his honor for his support of paleontology in Germany, specifically for founding a paleontological museum in his castle in Bedheim on July 1, 1934.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio fue nombrado en su honor por su apoyo a la paleontología en Alemania al fundar un museo paleontológico en su castillo en Bedheim, el 1 de julio de 1934.

facts.statement: Liliensternus specimens remained in Count Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern's castle until 1969, when they were transferred to the collection of the Natural History Museum in Berlin.
facts.quote: Los especímenes de Liliensternus permanecieron en el castillo de Hugo Rühle von Lilienstern hasta 1969, cuando fueron transferidos a la colección del Museo de Historia Natural de Berlín, su ubicación actual.

facts.statement: In 1993, Gilles Cuny and Peter Galton described a new species assigned to this genus, Liliensternus airelensis.
facts.quote: En 1993, Gilles Cuny y Peter Galton describieron una nueva especie que asignaron a este género, Liliensternus airelensis.

facts.statement: In 2007, Martin Ezcurra and Cuny reassigned the material of L. airelensis to their own genus, Lophostropheus.
facts.quote: en 2007, Martin Ezcurra y Cuny asignaron el material a su propio género, Lophostropheus.

facts.statement: Rowe discovered in 1989 that Liliensternus is more derived than Dilophosaurus.
facts.quote: Rowe en 1989 descubrió que Liliensternus se deriva más que Dilophosaurus.

facts.statement: Originally assigned to Halticosauridae, Liliensternus is now considered a basal member of Neotheropoda.
facts.quote: Originalmente asignado a los Halticosauridae, Liliensternus se considera hoy un miembro basal del Neotheropoda.

facts.statement: The only material from later strata assigned to this genus was discovered in 1913 in blue claystone of the Late Triassic Rhaetian stage in the Trossingen Formation of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, approximately 208 to 201 million years ago.
facts.quote: El único material asignado a este género de estratos posteriores se descubrió en 1913 en piedra de arcilla azul de la etapa rética del Triásico Tardío, en la Formación Trossingen de Sachsen-Anhalt, Alemania, hace aproximadamente 208 a 201 millones de años.

facts.statement: Liliensternus lived during the Norian to Rhaetian stages, from 227.3 to 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Rauhut and colleagues noted in 199 that the remains might represent a juvenile or subadult individual based on the presence of only two fused sacra and visible neurocentral sutures in the vertebrae.
facts.quote: Rauhut y colaboradores en 199 señalaron que los restos pueden representar un individuo juvenil o subadulto basado en la presencia de solo dos sacros fusionados y el hecho de que las suturas neurocentrales aún son visibles en las vértebras.

facts.statement: Liliensternus had five fingers with smaller fourth and fifth digits, representing a possible transitional stage between five-fingered Triassic theropods and three-fingered Jurassic theropods.
facts.quote: Liliensternus tiene cinco dedos, al igual que sus contemporáneos, pero sus dígitos cuarto y quinto son más pequeños que el resto, una posible etapa de transición entre los terópodos de cinco dedos del Triásico y los de tres dedos del Jurásico.
